To prove it, compress each subdivided 1-chain to a single edge when reading paths between original objects. The compression is unambiguous since all its interior vertices are private. Such an edge represents either an original edge or an interior spatial path of a 2-chart. Give the former its original length and the latter the common length of the exterior paths of that chart. The latter are translations of old 1-terms, both when subdividing an original 2-variable and when the 2-chart occurs recursively in a higher attachment. A generating 2-step replaces an exterior word by a private edge, one private edge by the next, or a private edge by an exterior word. All steps preserve length. Every declared 3-rule acts in a spatial window whose *initial and final paths consist entirely of original edges* after compression. Indeed they are the translated 1-boundaries of the type at which the 3-chain is constructed, shared by all its beads by globularity. Its temporal sides can be arbitrary histories there, including empty ones. Higher declarations introduce no further moves in dimension three. Replacing any private spatial edge by its chart's original source word also shows that reachability between original objects is unchanged.

For a composable pair choose a 2-chart in each of its two attachments, recursively if necessary. Take the last 2-step $q$ of the left chart and the first 2-step $p$ of the right chart. Insert the translated intervening path. In the initial spatial path of their square the left factor is a private edge just before $q$. In the final path the right factor is a private edge just after $p$. Mark a half-integer length coordinate inside each of these two factors. Positive integral lengths and length preservation place the marks in disjoint ordered intervals at the two ends of the square and allow the same coordinates to be read at each time in every proposed return. Each history starts with the left mark in the designated private edge and ends with it in the old exterior word. Until a step touches that mark the whole edge persists, and $q$ is its only outgoing step. The right mark starts in an old exterior word and ends in its designated private edge, so dually $p$ must be the last step touching it. This singles out one occurrence of each event even with identical variable labels elsewhere.

A declared rule whose window misses a mark cannot change any event touching it. A rule whose window contains the left mark cannot cover the first event touching that mark, or introduce one before it. At the start of such a replacement the window would still contain the private edge, but the rule starts on a word of original edges. At the right mark use the final word to exclude covering the last event or inserting one after it. This argument includes rules spanning both marks and rules applied at empty temporal windows. A forward square interchanges steps with disjoint windows, putting the spatially earlier one first. It preserves the identities of the distinguished events since two independent steps cannot both touch the same mark. If it interchanges the distinguished events themselves it puts $q$ first: the two windows contain the respective marks in that spatial order. Thus the reading with $q$ before $p$ cannot return to the reading with $p$ before $q$. ### Why the two conclusions cannot be combined

In fact **published strict units plus just the single word equality between the two readings of the ordinary binary interchange square fail in dimension four on one scalar**. Write $R(a,b),L(a,b)$ for the two readings in Rice's order and $s(a,b)$ for the raw head $R\to L$ over the generic two-bigon arity. The strict-unit normalizer gives the following three equalities in the two-scalar context:
$$
 E(a,b)\equiv_{su}s(a,b),\qquad
 R(a,b)\equiv_{su}a*_1 b,\qquad
 L(a,b)\equiv_{su}b*_1 a .
$$
Here $E$ is Rice's raw two-variable Eckmann–Hilton term from Response 1. The equalities are conversions, as witnessed by the well-typed identities in the checker linked below. Pruning, disc removal and endo-coherence removal are the published strict-unit rules used in this calculation. [Rice’s raw term](https://github.com/alexarice/catt-strict/blob/577993375ec7491b1b50c07dc58a0595c5fd58fc/examples/eh.catt) · [The two square readings](https://github.com/alexarice/catt-strict/blob/577993375ec7491b1b50c07dc58a0595c5fd58fc/examples/eh-common.catt)

Once $R=L$ is imposed at the generic square, congruence changes the head type of $s$ to $R\to R$ and published endo-coherence removal gives $s=1_R$. Equivalently, the binary clause (ii) for this same square gives $s=1_R$ directly. Specialize $b=a$ and use the displayed strict-unit equalities. The result is $E(a,a)=1_{a*_1a}$. Conversion of the identity supplies a 4-cell at this exact old type. The two-colour argument of Response 1 excludes either raw orientation: the diagonal braid exchanges the two positions and the identity fixes them. The two sets of low-data judgements alone already suffice, since the generic square has generating rank two and all three strict-unit judgements have generating rank two.

Both sets of equations are sound in the ordinary strict image, so Known 2 gives conservativity through dimension three even for the combined theory. Contexts with at most one declaration are empty or a point; full strict-image conversion is conservative there. Thus four is the least failing output degree and two is the least possible number of declarations for the combined theory. The least input rank at which allowing the two families together can fail is exactly two, since Response 25 covers their joint strict equations on graph data. For the individual binary surface the positional model of Response 4 still separates the diagonal braid from the identity. For the individual published theory its normal forms separate them. This is why the two different choices of base in the affirmative theorem matter.

Consequently there is a law-by-law classification for the joint calculation on planar data. Choose either published equality and any binary subset $S$. Close their judgements on 2-dimensional data under conversion, congruence and substitution in arbitrary contexts. This is universally conservative **if and only if $I\notin S$**. In the affirmative cases both families are contained in published insertion: pruning is its identity-insertion case, and it contains the associative and unital binary surface by the Setting. The insertion base above therefore interprets even the planar consequences derived using both families together. In the negative cases the single square and the strict-unit judgements already give the scalar counterexample. This also gives the same negative answer for the joint theories with no input restriction whenever $I\in S$.

**Validation.** In a scalar context with an additional 5-generator, the checker changed its attaching boundary using a square followed by its reverse. It transported the generator, corrected both 4-faces over the generic square, folded the two labels to the same scalar, and checked that the resulting 5-cell has the prescribed raw type and uses that generator once. Agda 2.8.0 checked this cell and the folded raw swap. Rice's checker at the linked revision accepted the three two-variable conversion witnesses under each of `--su` and `--sua`; in separate runs both modes rejected the proposed diagonal identity conversion. The extra single-square equality in the negative result is the mathematical use of the additional law. [Planar base checker](../../../tools/semistrict_surface_planar_base.py)

## Researcher Response 27

**For either published equality, every surface cell over a globular set of generators has a raw representative at any prescribed raw boundary representing its faces. The representative has the specified surface normal form.** This holds in every dimension, with repeated labels, endomorphisms and cycles in the generating globular set. In particular it applies simultaneously to a whole surface substitution. For the published theories, identity-class comparisons between pairs of raw terms suffice for Q1 in an arbitrary finite context. For **every binary surface in both kernels** as well as the published theories, any failure in degree $n$ already has a witness supported on one strict paste, with each $n$-generator used exactly once.

### Fitting a specified surface cell to an old boundary

Fix ordinary CaTT, a raw context $X$, and $R=su$ or $sua$. Write $N_R$ for the unique normal form. Let $p_X:H_X\to U F_R X$ send each raw cell to its surface class, where the right side has the underlying raw operations of the free surface model on the same declarations. A globular lifting problem for $p_X$ specifies a surface cell and a parallel pair of raw cells over its faces. Fix $n\ge1$. Then these two conditions are equivalent.

1. Every such problem through degree $n$ has a raw lift, with object lifts included.
2. For every $k<n$ and every ordered pair of literal parallel raw $k$-terms $a,b$ in $X$ with $N_R(a)=N_R(b)$, there is a raw cell $h:a\to b$ with $N_R(h)=N_R(1_a)$.

In degree zero objects are variables. For necessity, lift the surface identity at the two specified faces. For sufficiency, first observe how to fit a raw term $r$ whose surface class is the desired one to a prescribed old type. Work up its boundary starting at dimension zero. At stage $k$, the current and prescribed $k$-source have the same surface class, and are raw-parallel since all lower faces already agree literally. The same holds at the target. Use condition 2 in the two required orientations to obtain a cell from the prescribed source to the current source and a cell from the current target to the prescribed target. Paste these on the two sides of $r$ at cut $k$, using the standard three-factor padding composite. Its $k$-faces are now the prescribed ones, and every lower face stays fixed. In the surface the two comparisons are identities. Pruning the two identity arguments and evaluating the resulting disc gives exactly the previous surface cell. This is the calculation in Rice's proof for $P_{k+1}$ and works for any labels with these types and identity classes. For $k=0$ the endpoints already agree as variables, so the stage can also be skipped. After the last cut the term has the required literal type. [Rice, §4.5.1, Definitions 4.5.4–6 and proof of (4)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.17068#page=194)

It remains to produce the initial $r$, since a surface head can itself have a converted generic type. Induct on the expression for the surface term, proving lifting at *any* specified compatible raw boundary. A variable starts with its declaration. For a head on a pasting arity $P$, apply Rice's Theorem 4.5.3 to the surface head at the identity labelling of $P$. It supplies a raw term over $P$ in that surface class, possibly at a different raw writing of its type. Lift the actual input substitution one entry at a time in declaration order. For an entry its required old type is the type in $P$ evaluated on the raw entries already chosen. This represents its surface type because those entries have the specified classes. The induction applies to the entry, a proper argument expression, also when its dimension equals that of the enclosing term. The arity dimension bounds used here follow from fullness. At an operation the output degree is at least the tree height. At a coherence its boundary already visits the whole tree. Substitution into the generic raw representative produces $r$. Fitting it as above completes the induction. Conversion of its assigned type does not change the expression or its surface class. Thus the reduction uses Rice's theorem only on the generic arity, with no assumption about the support of a term in $X$. [Rice, Theorem 4.5.3 and §4.5.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.17068#page=194)

In particular, if published insertion first supplies a new inhabitant in degree $n$ in some context $X$, condition 2 fails there at some $k<n$. Condition 2 prescribes the normal form of the comparison between that pair. Conversely a failure of condition 2 alone detects failure to represent a *specified* class. Inhabitation in Q1 permits every class at the boundary.

### Separating occurrences before taking a normal form

Let $Z$ now be a globular set of generators, so its attaching faces are actual generating variables. Denote its free ordinary strict category by $FZ$. We use two properties of a globular relabelling $f:Y\to Z$, even when it identifies generators.

First, normalization of a well-typed surface term commutes with $f$. The relabelling acts on argument variables and leaves every bound arity and its generic head type fixed. In the reduction system a disc is recognized on the generic arity and an endo-coherence on its generic type. Pruning recognizes an identity head in an argument. Standard insertion recognizes an identity or standard composite there and tests the heights of the branches of the two trees. None tests equality of two ambient labels. Inspection of the head and induction on its arguments, including substitutions, show that a normal expression stays normal. Relabelling its reduction sequence gives the same reduct at each corresponding position because the exterior substitution in insertion is defined on the trees. Uniqueness of normal forms proves the assertion. In particular two *different* ambient labels becoming equal does not create a generic endo-coherence redex. Second, two well-typed surface expressions over $Y$ that relabel to the **same syntax** and have the same lifted ordinary strict value must be the same syntax (using bound positions for arity variables). For a variable this is the cartesian unit of the free strict category monad. At a head, both expressions have the identical generic head. Its ordinary strict positional shape is the whole arity, including for an identity on a full-support cell. This holds with converted head boundaries as well because ordinary strict evaluation respects conversion and full support determines the visited subtree. The strict argument labelling downstairs is read from the common expression. This labelling and the given lifted cell determine the strict values of *each* argument upstairs by the cartesian multiplication of the free strict category monad, just as in Response 4. Induction on the proper argument expressions proves equality, without an existence assumption about lifting a surface derivation. Together the two properties show that two surface terms of equal strict value upstairs are $R$-equal whenever their relabellings are $R$-equal, by syntax uniqueness applied to their normal forms. [Positional lifting and support](#researcher-response-4) · [Leinster, Appendix F](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0305049)

Take literal parallel raw $u,v$ over $Z$ with the same $R$-normal form. Their common ordinary strict value consists of a finite positional pasting shape $P$, its generic cell $c$ (identity-padded to the given degree), and a globular labelling $f:P\to Z$. By raw positional lifting in Response 4, lift $u$ and $v$ along $f$ with strict value $c$. The lifts $\bar u,\bar v$ are literally parallel because their faces lift the same old face with the same strict value, hence agree by uniqueness. Both terms have full support in $P$ by Response 9. The preceding reflection argument gives $\bar u\equiv_R\bar v$ **in $P$**. Therefore the raw coherence on $P$ from $\bar u$ to $\bar v$ is accepted, and congruence in its generic type followed by endo-coherence removal makes it $R$-equal to $1_{\bar u}$. Relabel it back to $Z$. This proves condition 2 in every dimension and also gives the other orientation by exchanging the terms. It is essential to perform endo-coherence removal before specializing the generic head. The same construction on a point handles dimension zero.

It follows that $p_Z$ is a globular trivial fibration. For an assignment of any raw computad’s generators to surface cells over $Z$, lift each entry at the boundary determined by its predecessors. The argument also works relative to a previously lifted subcomputad. It preserves each entry's surface normal form. Furthermore, the square for $UF_R(-)\to F(-)$ at any globular relabelling is a pullback on cells. For existence, first lift the given downstairs surface cell to a raw representative, lifting its globe of faces in order. Lift that representative at the given upstairs strict value by Response 4 and take its surface class. Uniqueness is the reflection argument above. In particular identifying labels loses no additional information once their positions in the strict cell are specified.

For either kernel and any of its binary surfaces, or for either published ordinary theory, let $Z$ be a dependency-closed subcomputad of $X$. Then the square

We call such a strict cell supported in $Z$.

Here is a proof of the upper inclusion that does not require a normal-form theorem for the binary laws. This is the positional description in Response 4, including a point for the support of an identity on a vertex. Clamp the spine to the subinterval. In a column outside it send each arrow to the identity on its clamped vertex and each higher generator to the iterated identity there. In a traversed column suspend the recursively constructed child retraction. The assignments fit at the common spine vertices. They use only variables and their iterated identities and fix every variable in $Q$. This proves the word retraction in both kernels, with no equational laws imposed.

Construct a surface model above $FX$ by induction on cell dimension. Over a strict cell supported in $Z$ take the cells of $UF_S Z$ with that strict value, with their existing faces. Over any other strict cell take exactly one cell for each compatible choice of lifted boundary (one choice for a vertex). All the surface laws hold in the ordinary strict target. For a head with a specified labelling, if its output strict value is supported in $Z$, **all** its input labels have strict values supported there. Indeed its generic ordinary strict cell visits every slot, and the support of the labelled paste is the union of the supports of those labels. This is the full-arity property in Response 4, also for the ordinary projection of a directed total. At a converted generic boundary strict interpretation still has the designated total or full identity. Use the given surface operation in $UF_S Z$ on such a tuple. It has the already interpreted faces, by induction on their expressions. Otherwise use the unique lift at the interpreted boundary. These definitions compose with substitution by evaluating on the resulting tuple. At congruent head types the designated strict values agree and so do the already interpreted faces. In the supported case one uses head congruence of the given surface algebra.

An equation between two binary words can involve *unused* variables of its ambient arity. If their common strict value on a tuple is supported in $Z$, restrict the tuple to the support $Q$ of the common generic ordinary strict cell. All entries needed there are supported in $Z$ by the strict substitution formula. The two words involve only $Q$, by raw support reflection. Substitution of the word retraction in the generic equality in the free word algebra proves their word law over $Q$. Thus evaluation on the restricted tuple gives equal cells of $UF_S Z$. For clause (ii) the coherence uses the entire arity and the same argument uses the whole tuple. For the published rules use the disc, the generic endo-coherence, or the single spliced arity of an insertion (the pruned arity for an identity insertion). In the last case the right-hand head uses all labels of that arity and the left-hand side uses their exterior and interior substitutions. Both therefore agree by the rule in $UF_S Z$. In all cases, at an output strict value outside $FZ$, equal strict values and equal lifted faces suffice by uniqueness. The faces in clause (ii) use the word equality just verified. These checks give the simultaneous interpretation of formation, equality and conversion.

Interpret the generators of $X$ in this model, taking those in $Z$ to their own classes, and each remaining generator to the lift of its strict generator at its interpreted boundary. On $UF_S Z$ the composite of weakening and this interpretation is the inclusion of the supported cells, so weakening is injective. Conversely any surface term over $X$ with a supported strict value is in its image. For a variable this is the support test. At a head all argument cells are supported, so each has an antecedent by induction on the expression. Their antecedents agree on the required boundaries, since weakening is injective and the generic arity has globular incidences. Apply the same surface head to those antecedents. Its weakening is the original term class. This proves the pullback assertion.

Consequently, for a specified surface class at an old boundary, the existence of a raw representative of that class is exactly the same in $X$ and in the support of its strict paste. Its raw faces belong to this subcomputad by Response 9. Any raw representative has the same strict value and hence strengthens there. The upper inclusion reflects equality of classes, and weakening proves the converse. A failure to represent a *specified class* persists under every extension by fresh declarations, even one that introduces another inhabitant of the same old type. For published units or insertion, a class with globular attaching faces throughout its support always lifts by the preceding theorem, regardless of the rest of $X$. For ordinary binary surfaces, a putative failure of *inhabitation* also restricts to this support, since any raw filler of any class there would weaken to $X$. ### Reducing possible counterexamples to terms linear in their top generators

For every surface just considered there is a further reduction in an arbitrary lower-dimensional context. Fix $n>0$ and any raw $(n-1)$-skeleton. Form extensions by $n$-generators with specified old attaching types. An occurrence below refers to a free $n$-variable in the argument expression, counting repetitions. There are none in the inferred boundary or in an argument of smaller dimension. Distinct occurrences can therefore be replaced independently by new $n$-generators with the same literal declarations, preserving raw typing for a raw term and surface typing for a surface term. To see this after localization to the support, first send every used generator to a designated first copy by raw substitution. This supplies the original typing derivation on the larger list of copies. Change the chosen occurrence in each argument recursively. Its replacement variable has the identical raw declared type. Every required entry type and every inferred result type uses ambient terms only below degree $n$, so these types and the conversions between them stay literally the same. The generic head has its own bound context and stays fixed.

For the two published theories, normalization transports these occurrences bijectively. At an $n$-head of arity dimension less than $n$ there are no $n$-occurrences. Otherwise they are exactly the disjoint lists from its $n$-slots. Disc removal carries the top argument once. An endo-coherence head of degree $n$ uses a full $(n-1)$-face and so has no $n$-slot. At an insertion the enlarged tree retains each outside top slot once and the replacement branch contributes each top slot of its inserted tree once. This follows directly by splicing the child lists at the branching path. Shared faces of the branch have dimension below its leaf and cannot duplicate a top slot. The inserted tree has no $n$-slots for a lower-dimensional entry or for an identity in degree $n$. This includes pruning. Reducing a generic head type affects none of the argument occurrences. Structural reductions compose the bijections inside the affected argument. When all occurrences receive fresh generator names before normalization, every reduction uses the same tree tests and carries each fresh name to exactly one place. Uniqueness of the resulting coloured normal form makes the matching independent of a choice of reduction sequence. The argument requires no restrictions on the attaching types in the fixed skeleton. [Insertion labelling and exterior substitution, Definitions 21–23](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.05303#page=17)

This gives two tests relevant to the unrestricted question.

- Universal **inhabitation** conservativity in degree $n$, for each binary surface in each kernel and each published theory, is equivalent to its restriction to proposed surface witnesses in which each declared $n$-generator occurs exactly once, and whose strict support is the whole context. Indeed localize a failing witness and its old boundary as above. Copy each top generator once per occurrence, with the same lower-dimensional type. Label the witness by these distinct copies and take its support. The old boundary is unchanged since it lies in the lower skeleton. A raw filler of any class in the new context would give one in the original context by the raw substitution folding the copies. For a published theory the witness may also be required to be in normal form, since giving each occurrence its own name leaves a normal expression normal. For a binary surface no normalization is used. This deduction also covers witnesses with no $n$-generators.
- To test condition 2 **universally** in rank $k>0$, it suffices to test raw parallel pairs in which each $k$-generator occurs once on each side and occupies the same position in their common coloured normal form. Give each occurrence in the common uncoloured normal form its own fresh declaration and pull the names back along the occurrence bijections for the two raw terms. The resulting raw pair has unchanged lower faces and equal coloured normal forms. An identity-class comparison for the coloured pair specializes to one for the original pair. One can also pass to the support throughout. Thus if Q1 fails in degree $n$ for published insertion there is an identity-class obstruction of this form in some rank $k<n$ (degree zero has no obstruction). An arbitrary-context proof of this linear identity-class test in all ranks would prove the stronger rehydration statement and hence Q1 for insertion.

The condition for the directed result uses the directed strict image.

This is an arity of dimension at most $k$, and applying the retraction preserves the equality of the respective strict values. Its labelling is raw. Two-way raw reachability is closed under replacing $k$-dimensional arguments of a raw $k$-head. To see why, vary one $k$-slot of its arity by a single directed $(k+1)$-cell. The slot is maximal. Raising it replaces its generator by two parallel copies joined by a new generator and leaves the other maximal labels fixed. This is a pasting arity with two copies of the original labelling, and the two copies of the head have identical literal boundaries. In the ordinary strict image its $k$-paste can be lifted to a $(k+1)$-paste from the first copy to the second. For the directed kernel, when $k\ge2$ a $k$-head with a $k$-slot must be a total. The column containing that slot already contributes $k-1$ to the tensor degree, leaving every other column stationary. After the raise its column is still the only active factor. For detail on passing from generators to cells, lift a pasted expression recursively. At cut zero split the given input path at the two factors' lengths. Units split off an empty word or pass the given order unchanged at the applicable cut. This proves independence of expression by induction on dimension and the strict equations; when proving it at a given dimension the lifted boundaries have already been computed in lower dimensions. Conversely, lifting the expression obtained by forgetting any coloured expression recovers it, by the rule for generators and recursion on its cuts. ### The parallel faces of the directed cube

There is precisely one unordered pair of distinct parallel $(k-1)$-cells in $Q_k$, the two faces of its top atom. To see this use the nonnegative chain tableaux of the directed cube. That coefficient is at most one by Steiner's multiplicity theorem. The two rows of degree $j<k$ of the top atom itself each have one term for every such $J$, and their two terms are distinct. Indeed the tensor atom formula chooses the free interval edge at the positions of $J$. At each omitted position take the endpoint with the row's sign reversed once for each preceding free edge. Exchanging the sign changes every omitted bit. This also gives the two endpoint vertices in degree zero. For parallel $(k-1)$-cells the difference of top chains is a cycle. A zero difference gives equal tableaux since the lower rows are shared. For a nonzero difference, the projection bound just proved forces the multiple to be $+1$ or $-1$ and the two top chains to be precisely the two hemisphere chains. Their common lower rows are forced as well. At each descent the difference of the next two rows is the differential of the known row. For each subset of the lower degree the two terms of the standard atom there are distinct and exhaust the permitted coefficient on each side. Thus that differential already determines both rows. Its two $(k-1)$-cells in $Q_k$ are parallel and distinct. By the parallel-face result they must be exactly $u,v$ in that order. The contextual new generator giving this move consequently has strict source $g^+$ and target $g^-$. In a bare chart the exterior stationary whiskers of a matching declaration must both be empty. The 1-source then reconstructs the entire bare chart by the right-to-left calculation, so one declaration can supply the required move for at most one chart. One declaration at each reverse raw type suffices by direct use. This proves the exact count, including the scalar formula. ## Researcher Response 33

**In ordinary CaTT all eight binary surfaces and both published surfaces are conservative through dimension five in every finite context without 1- or 2-generators.** The 3-generators may be scalars at iterated identities. Their attaching terms can have arbitrary raw writings, and the 4- and 5-generators can have arbitrary boundaries. Full ordinary strict-image conversion already fails in dimension five on a single such scalar.

More generally, suppose the first positive generator degree is $n\ge3$ and the next occupied degree is $h>n$, with $h=\infty$ allowed. The bound through which all ten surfaces are conservative is at least
$$
                            \min(2n-1,h+1).
$$
On the generating $n$-skeleton itself, an old $(n+2)$-type has a raw inhabitant exactly when its two $(n+1)$-faces induce the same permutation of the individual scalar occurrences, after identifying the source and target occurrences at the common boundary. The permutation test below computes this criterion with repeated as well as distinct generators. The bound $2n-1$ is sharp for the comparison *with permutations*. A higher homotopy group first escapes that comparison at a specified old $2n$-type.

### Occurrences of arbitrary rank in the surface laws

Fix a degree $n\ge2$ and a set of colours. We construct two ordinary surface models. Each has a single cell in each degree below $n$. In the binary model an $n$-cell is a finite table of lists of colours indexed by finite binary strings. In the published model it is one list of colours. In either model an $(n+1)$-cell is a colour-preserving bijection of the positions in its two incident $n$-cells. It may change both the address and the index in a list. Above bijections use only iterated identities.

For the binary model interpret a degree-$n$ head by its ordinary strict $n$-generator occurrences. A binary composite at cut $n-1$ concatenates the lists pointwise. At a binary cut $j<n-1$, prefix the addresses of each operand of degree $n$ by its side, 0 or 1. This includes a whiskering with just one such operand. For other arities concatenate pointwise in a fixed order of the strict occurrences. For the published model, at every head concatenate in the planar order of the $n$-generators visited by the strict paste. On a tree of height $n$ this is the left-to-right order of its depth-$n$ branches, and on a tree of smaller height the list is empty. These choices depend only on the arity and designated strict cell. Changing a generic head type by conversion preserves them.

For both models, higher heads are determined by their action on individually distinguished occurrences. On a globular arity form the equivalence classes of $n$-generators joined by $(n+1)$-generators. A strict $n$-cell uses at most one occurrence from each class. In each class the directed graph of transports, after identifying parallel generating transports joined by an $(n+2)$-generator, is a string. The corresponding bijections are equal for any admissible labelling since the only cells above bijections are identities. Start with distinct auxiliary colours for all positions in one table or list per class, disjoint across classes, and transport those colours along the string by the given bijections. Each evaluated $n$-expression contains precisely the occurrences contributed by its strict top chain, by induction on the head and the substitution. The two $n$-faces of an $(n+1)$-head use the same classes. Matching the auxiliary colours therefore gives a unique bijection between them. Its underlying map is independent of the auxiliary names. An $(n+2)$-head has parallel bijections which preserve these same distinct colours, so they agree. This defines all head operations, including those at a converted generic type. The operations act on an evaluated tuple, so substitution composes. Recolouring leaves the underlying positions and bijections fixed. [Slot and transport lemmas in arbitrary degree](../answered/relative-coherence-all-dimensions-r3-2026-11-19.md#a-catt-model-of-lists-and-bijections) · [The degree-two construction](#researcher-response-4)

For the binary equations the essential verification is at degree $n$. Read the literal $(n-1)$-source of a generic $n$-word as its constructor tree. At each leaf that is an $(n-1)$-variable record the path of generating $n$-steps changing that leaf. A generating $n$-variable supplies one step from its source leaf to its target leaf. An identity has empty paths. At a lower cut the cut node remains in the source and target trees and the paths take the corresponding left and right addresses. An operand of degree at most $n-1$ stays stationary with all its paths empty. At the top cut the two words have the very same intervening face, so concatenate the paths leaf by leaf. These rules prove by induction that the target tree has the same shape, with exactly the indicated changes of leaf labels.

Two raw-parallel $n$-words on a globular arity with equal ordinary strict value have the same path at **each** leaf. Indeed the occurrences of $(n-1)$-variables in their common source are precisely its top chain, by the binary and identity formulas. Apply the slot lemma one degree lower. Distinct such leaves belong to distinct transport classes for the $n$-steps. Thus the strict $n$-chain gives the multiset of steps at each individual leaf. The order is forced because the sources and targets follow the directed string in that class. Parallel alternative edges have the same endpoints, but the chain records the name of the edge used, and the string traverses that position at most once. Leaves inside a stationary identity contribute nothing. On any labelling, the interpreted table is obtained by concatenating the input tables along these paths and prefixing by their leaf addresses. The addresses of different leaves are prefix-incomparable. This proves (i) even for the full set of laws and for auxiliary-colour labellings. At degree $n+1$ the two parallel words induce bijections that agree on the distinguished positions. In (ii), a degree-$n$ coherence over equal words has empty top chain, and a degree-$(n+1)$ coherence over equal $n$-words fixes every position by the equality on the refined labelling. In the other degrees the equations follow from the singleton lower cells or uniqueness at the boundary. This verifies the full surface theory under substitution, also inside head types.

For the published laws, disc removal returns the input list. An endo-coherence of degree $n$ has no $n$-occurrence. At a degree-$n$ insertion the order on the joined arity is the old planar order with the selected branch replaced in place by the planar order of the inner tree. Descending along the branch changes only the chosen child at each shared trunk level. At the splice the inner sequence of branches replaces one branch between the unchanged prefix and suffix. For a selected maximal slot of degree $n$ the exterior substitution gives its standard composite of the inner slots in exactly this order. If the inner height is smaller there are no $n$-slots in that block. A selected maximal slot of degree below $n$ changes no depth-$n$ entry. These observations include identity pruning and the disc case of the standard term. They prove the rank-$n$ insertion equality for any outer head and any labels. In degree $n+1$ compute both sides on the joined arity with the refined colours. Their evaluated endpoints agree by the transported type and the rank-$n$ calculation. Both maps preserve the distinguished colours, so they are the same bijection. A disc gives the given bijection by transport, and a generic endo-coherence on equal faces fixes all positions on the refined labelling. In higher degrees only the boundaries matter. Thus the list model carries the published insertion action, including strict units. Each model separately defines a raw map out of the scalar computad by assigning a singleton of its own colour to every generating scalar. [Insertion and the exterior substitution, §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.05303)

### Distinguishing top-generator occurrences in every dimension

There is a consequence for *arbitrary* attaching terms. Let $Z$ be a finite ordinary computad generated through $n$, and $Y$ the same lower skeleton with a set of copies of its $n$-generators at their original raw types. The copy map $f:Y\to Z$ can omit generators. Write $L$ for the selected free surface model, $Q(C)$ for the appropriate occurrence model above, and $C_Y,C_Z$ for the sets of top generator names. Evaluate each such generator as its named singleton and every lower generator as the unique cell in its degree. Then there is an isomorphism of globular sets in **all** degrees
$$
 LY\ \cong\ LZ\times_{Q(C_Z)} Q(C_Y).
$$
Consequently any failure of conservativity on $Z$ in degree $k\ge n$ has a failure over a context of copies in which each top generator occurs exactly once in the witness's degree-$n$ source, counting positions in its table or list. At $k=n$ count the witness itself. At $k>n$ this separates occurrences in the boundary, even when the witness uses high-dimensional coherences and the top generators are attached at identities or composites.

To verify the isomorphism we give the splitting calculation for this square. At a head of degree $n$, every $n$-slot of its arity supplies its input positions exactly once, with the injections into the output specified by the table or list formula. A recolouring of the output restricts uniquely to all those inputs. No colour is needed in smaller degrees. At any head of degree $k>n$ its iterated $n$-source uses exactly one generating $n$-variable from every transport class of the arity. For this last fact collapse each class to one $n$-generator and send all higher generators to iterated identities on it, retaining the lower generators. This is a strict globular labelling, since higher variables have parallel variable faces. The designated ordinary value visits the entire arity. By the strict support union formula its image visits each collapsed $n$-generator. Above rank $n$ that image is an iterated identity, hence its $n$-source already visits every collapsed generator. The slot lemma gives the at-most-once assertion before collapse. [Full arity and support under substitution](#researcher-response-27)

A lift of the output in $Q(C_Y)$ prescribes colours on its $n$-source occurrences. Read them back through the injections for that source expression (at degree $n$, every occurrence of a used $n$-variable has its own block of positions). Transport these colours along the labelled bijections of each string. This uniquely recolours every input of dimension $n$, including the middle variables which the $n$-source does not itself use. The unique lift of each higher input keeps its underlying bijection at rank $n+1$ and takes the identity tower on it above that rank. Evaluating on this lifted tuple gives the requested output lift by the distinguished-colour definition of the head. The argument also covers a head whose arity has height below $n$, where there are no positions. For nested heads, splitting twice gives the input colours obtained by evaluating first, since both assign each distinguished position its prescribed colour, with every intermediate bijection acting by transport. For a boundary expression using only part of an arity this argument applies on the support of its generic ordinary strict cell, which has the word retraction of Response 27.

For clarity about conversion, construct a surface algebra over $Q(C_Z)$ by the family construction of Response 32, now indexing a family over $q$ by the lifts of $q$ along $Q(C_Y)\to Q(C_Z)$. Its values are cells of $LY$ over the indicated index, with the chosen compatible boundary families as there. For a head use the split just constructed and apply that head in $LY$. Splitting under substitution and restriction to the boundary give its typing. For a generic binary word equation on its common support, splitting the two outputs produces the same recoloured inputs. Indeed the word law holds when each position of each transport class receives its own auxiliary name. Thus the two words use the very same named occurrences at each output position. Propagating those colours back gives the same tuple on the support. Apply the restricted word law in $LY$ there. Clause (ii) uses the entire supported tuple. For a published insertion the right-hand head visits every slot of the joined tree, and splitting its exterior and interior substitutions on the left returns those labels by the planar-order and bijection calculations. For pruning use the pruned tree, for disc removal the single label, and for a generic endo-coherence the supported tuple on its arity. In the latter case generic head congruence and its premise hold in the given algebra $LY$. This verifies the family action with all the required equations. Below rank $n$ a generator receives its original cell over the unique index. A top generator receives the family of its named copies, well typed since its raw attaching expressions have smaller degree and are shared. Evaluating $LZ$ in this algebra gives the inverse map in the displayed formula. Relabelling recovers the original tuple at each head, and the input colours of an existing upstairs expression are the unique split of its evaluated colours. Induction on the expressions gives both inverse identities.

For the consequence, assign a fresh copy of its top generator to each position at the $n$-source of a surface witness. For $k>n$ transport these colours using its bijection, and use its forced identities higher up. For $k=n$ assign the colours directly on the value. Lift the surface witness by the isomorphism. To lift its old boundary in the **raw** theory, take the prescribed copy at a variable and retain each raw head with the same split on its tuple. At a shared face the two lifted raw writings agree literally, since the original writing and the assigned colours determine the lift uniquely by this recursion. In particular these lifts have precisely the surface faces of the lifted witness. A raw filler there would relabel to a raw filler at the original boundary. This proves the consequence with no normal-form assumption on the binary surface. It explains why an obstruction based solely on folding two top-generator names cannot distinguish surface inhabitation from raw inhabitation once the occurrence bijection has been fixed.

### The raw scalar mapping space and its first homotopy group

First take a single object and a finite set $C$ of degree-$n$ generators, with no others. Write $B$ for this computad. The realization of $H_B$ is the $n$-fold delooping of the free little-$n$-cubes algebra on the discrete space $C$. Here is the universal-property calculation. With the image $x$ of the object fixed, a map from the cellular realization specifies one $n$-endomorphism of the iterated identity of $x$ for each element of $C$, with the full space of such choices. The attaching maps for other raw writings of the boundaries give the same derived pushout because they factor through the raw algebra on the single point, whose realization is terminal. For a pointed target the underlying space of its $n$-fold endomorphisms represents exactly these choices (take the space of objects and equivalences of the final hom). The $n$-fold delooping–endomorphism adjunction, followed by the free-algebra adjunction, gives the same mapping space for the proposed delooping. This calculation can be performed in $(\infty,n)$-categories because they contain the point, the $n$-globe and its boundary. Their inclusion into higher categories preserves the colimit since it has the right adjoint taking the invertible core above $n$. This identifies the generator maps as well as the object. When decoding a tuple, the incidence types can be checked in the lower degrees already constructed: their encodings are equal there by typing of the original tuple, and injectivity in those degrees identifies their decodings.

Conversely the classification exhausts the normal expressions, and parsing recovers every encoded normal form. This proves the free-algebra assertion in each dimension. In particular a choice of images of the symbols with the specified faces in a strict groupoid extends to a map of raw fixed-hom algebras.

### Which generators can occur in a face?

Put an order on the $2n$ labels by declaring $(j,\epsilon)<(l,\delta)$ whenever $j<l$, with either sign allowed. The only relation at the same height is equality. **Every generator in the decoded faces of a generator with label $\alpha$ has label at least $\alpha$.** This includes all occurrences inside their composite subexpressions.

Here are the strict and syntactic checks behind the assertion. Mark two distinct $n$-slots in a tree. Their label is the depth of their last common vertex and their left-to-right order, using the two particle names to read the sign. Under a strict labelling into another globular tree, suppose the two slots of an expression carry the two different marked events of the target. Its split in the expression has label at least their split in the target. It suffices to use the $n$-source and truncate the target tree at $n$, identifying its transports. At a cut of depth zero the two contributing paths traverse disjoint consecutive intervals of the target spine. The marked events must be in different target columns and in the indicated order. Conversely, if the two marked events of the target lie in a single column, a cut separating them must have positive depth. Project the contributing paths to that column and repeat one level lower, using the description of strict homs on a globular tree as products along a spine interval. This proves the inequality, with order preservation at equal depth. The same argument allows stationary factors: each factor which carries a mark must traverse its marked column. Positional support ensures that a single occurrence in the target is used only once in the strict reading. In its ambient argument subexpressions, including the expression itself, every head where the two particles belong to distinct $n$-slots must split them with label at least $\alpha$. Expressions with fewer occurrences impose no condition. In a generic tree labelled by such a tuple, require also the bound on the split of its two occupied slots if there are two. Then evaluating any generic expression on the tuple preserves the condition. Indeed, inspect its heads before substitution. Two marks arriving via distinct slots of the tuple satisfy the just-proved strict inequality at every head separating them. Marks arriving through one slot of the tuple travel together in the generic calculation, and any separation inside its actual labels was already checked. This applies also to the iterated faces, by the transport strings. Substitution copies actual expressions into variable positions and leaves their internal splits intact.

The condition persists during normalization. Disc removal selects the specified argument. Endo removal uses the instantiated generic boundary, to which the preceding paragraph applies, and takes its identity. In a pruning or insertion the new argument entries are inherited from the participating tuples. For the new head inspect the truncated spliced tree. At a splice the inner list of children replaces one child in place. Above the splice both trees descend the same unary trunk in the inner tree. Thus two marks inherited from different exterior branches have their former divergence depth and order, including when one comes from the replacement of the selected branch. Two marks in different interior branches have their divergence depth and order in the inner tree. If the splice is above degree $n$ in the globular dimension, its common ancestor at depth $n$ remains a single slot. An empty replacement carries no particle of its own; in an identity above $n$ the retained lower slot carries its existing particles. These are all cases by the two clauses of the tree insertion recursion. A reduction in a bound type leaves the ambient split unchanged. Starting with a generator on $P_j$ and its singleton labels therefore gives the asserted bound on its normalized faces. This argument does not assume that a specialized reduction can itself be performed on the original generic tree. [Tree splice and labelling formulas](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.05303#page=17)

Let $K$ be the order complex of these labels. It is the join of $n$ copies of the two-point set, hence the boundary sphere of the $n$-dimensional cross-polytope. Switching the particle names acts antipodally. The upper set of a label $\alpha$ has a least vertex $\alpha$, so its order complex $K_\alpha$ is a cone.

For a subcomplex $E$ use the strict abelian chain groupoid $G(E)$ of its integral simplicial chains with augmentation one at objects. Concretely an $i$-cell is a signed chain tableau with rows $(c_l^-,c_l^+)$ for $0\le l\le i$, equal top entries, augmentation one in row zero, and $\partial c_{l+1}^{\pm}=c_l^+-c_l^-$. Faces truncate and select the indicated entry. Composition adds tableaux and subtracts the identity extension of the common seam. These formulas are the chain-complex construction of a strict higher category with all chain signs allowed, so all arrows have inverses. In a cone any two parallel tableaux have a filler: the difference of the prescribed top chains is an augmented cycle and coning it supplies a chain with that boundary. These choices may be made within the cone in all dimensions. [Steiner, chain tableaux and the $\lambda,\nu$ adjunction](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0403237)

Send each degree-zero symbol with label $\alpha$ to its vertex. Inductively send a higher symbol to a filler in $G(K_\alpha)$. Its boundary is already there by the bound on faces and the inclusions $K_\beta\subseteq K_\alpha$ for $\beta\ge\alpha$. Strict composition and identities stay in this subgroupoid. Swapping $a,b$ acts freely on the symbols: the two distinct variable names exchange places in their normal expressions. Choose a filler on one representative and its antipodal image on the other. By the presentation just proved this gives an equivariant map from the published two-particle fixed hom to $G(K)$. Composing with the raw-to-surface map gives an equivariant raw map.

Write $m=n-1$. On realization the raw source component is $\operatorname{Conf}_2(\mathbb R^n)\simeq S^m$, equivariantly for particle exchange, by the free little-cubes calculation. Its difference direction is the antipodal sphere coordinate. The realization of $G(K)$ is $(m-1)$-connected with $\pi_m=\mathbb Z$. Moreover there is a canonical equivariant map from $|K|$ to it inducing an isomorphism on $\pi_m$. To verify these statements, its Street nerve has $r$-simplices the augmentation-preserving chain maps $C_*(\Delta^r)\to C_*(K)$. Indeed the oriental is the category of the simplex chains, its linearization recovers those chains, and all signs are allowed in the target. This nerve is the augmentation-one part of the Dold–Kan simplicial group of $C_*(K)$. A choice of vertex identifies that part with the simplicial group of the reduced chain complex. The canonical map sends a simplex to its chain map. On normalized chains it is the linearization map, taking a fundamental cycle to that very cycle. This gives the asserted generator by the Dold–Kan identification of homotopy and homology. Realization of the strict groupoid as a weak category gives this space by the strict nerve comparison. The two differences on the top discs are related by the involution, which acts by a sign on $\mathbb Z$. Their total contribution on the fundamental cycle is even. The canonical coefficient is one. This proof applies to a map in the homotopy theory of spaces with involution as well: the sphere with its free cell structure is cofibrant for equivariant maps with underlying weak equivalences. The raw map above therefore induces an injection on $\pi_m$. In particular a surface filler cannot connect two old $m$-discs in the fixed hom whose relative difference is a nonzero element of that group. ### Cutting an arity at its one positive input

Here is a construction on an arbitrary ordinary raw algebra $Y$. Make a new globular set $W_n(Y)$ with one cell in each degree below $n$. Its $n$-fold hom is a disjoint union indexed by a nonnegative integer weight. In weight one use $Y$ itself. In weight zero and in each weight greater than one use a terminal globular set. Thus below degree $n$ the single cells serve as the poles of all the summands.

Weights have their ordinary strict interpretation in the $n$-fold delooping of the additive monoid $\mathbb N$ with identity higher cells. In a tuple on a tree $P$ each subtree at depth $n$ has a weight: all its vertices, which are $n$-variables of $P$, have that weight because successive vertices are joined by higher labels. The weight of a full head in degree at least $n$ is the sum of these weights, one summand per subtree, by the full positional support and the transport-string calculation of Response 33. For an expression of partial support the same rule applies on its strict positional arity. Both assertions include identity padding in the strict reading.

For output of weight one there is therefore a unique selected subtree $T$. Follow its $n$ child indices from the root of $P$. At each child index take the ordinary directed cut of Response 11, colouring the spine vertices before this child by zero and the others by one. For a degree-$n$ head this returns the object label at the selected slot. In degree $n+l$ it returns an ordinary expression of degree $l$ on $T$; evaluate it in $Y$ at the retained labels. They all have weight one. Use the unique value at every other weight and below degree $n$. These are cuts on the **generic arity**. The ambient one-object computad need not admit any nonconstant cut on its objects.

To check typing and substitution, fix a weighted tuple on $P$ and a supported subexpression of weight one. Its ordinary strict positional arity contains exactly one of its own depth-$n$ slots contributing weight one. Under the labelling this is the slot through which the selected occurrence enters. At the root, substitution concatenates the intervals of columns in the ordinary strict paths. The selected column belongs to exactly one of these intervals; the selected column of that factor is its preimage cut. For a head of positive local degree, taking its cut restricts its generic type and keeps precisely the labels in that column, by the cut-substitution formula. For a crossing path it just selects the corresponding edge label. Apply this calculation on the retained child, successively down the $n$ levels. Thus cutting an expression on $P$ and interpreting its cut agrees with interpreting its constituent heads on their selected subtrees. The same calculation on a face restricts the selected labelling to that face; above $n$ both faces have the same weight. This proves the boundary formula, commutation with substitution and naturality in raw algebra maps $Y\to Y'$. In a suspended head on $\Sigma^n T$ the $n$ cuts recover the original head on $T$ literally. In particular the raw fixed hom in weight one is the original raw algebra, including its choices of coherences. [Ordinary cut and substitution](../answered/relative-coherence-all-dimensions-r7-2026-11-20.md#researcher-response-4) · [Slots and full positional support](#researcher-response-33)

For the published theories the construction on a surface algebra gives a surface algebra with exactly this raw action. Indeed check each rule in the common arity carrying its two labellings. At weight one each successive cut takes an insertion to the equality proved in Response 12, using the common joined arity and the cut pulled back along the exterior substitution. The verification for **strict units alone** needs only pruning, disc and endo removal. At one cut, pruning a stationary column or a peak within it leaves the selected child and its labelling fixed; below a crossing column the retained peak and its projection substitution are the lower pruning. A pruned generating edge at the root, labelled by an identity, cannot cross the cut pulled back from the pruned arity. When the selected child becomes a point the path rule selects its vertex, and the linear-disc cases use strict-unit disc trivialisation. Disc and endo rules restrict to their respective rules or vertex selection. These checks use the generic equality on the smaller tree, so they apply again at the next selected child. In every other weight equality follows from uniqueness and the lower boundary equalities. This gives the simultaneous interpretation for converted generic types and labellings as well. For a binary $S$ put $T=S$ for the six choices in the equivalence and $T=S\cup\{U\}$ for the two exceptional choices. Use $Y$ with the lower $T^+$ action of Response 15, where the superscript adjoins unary disc removal. On the supported generic arity of (i) the two projected words agree at each cut under the $T^+$ word calculation there. More precisely, one cut translates a $T^+$ derivation to a $T^+$ derivation at the selected child, preserving the raw restriction on old expressions. A positive cut lowers its index, a spatial product selects and pads its crossing operand, and the disc rule handles the resulting unary heads. For spatial whiskering interchange the stationary steps on the two sides can be absorbed by $U$ when interchange is required. Clause (ii) restricts to the lower coherence equation after these word equalities. An unused slot in (i) is handled by first restricting the word law to its common strict support using the word retraction of Response 27. This deals even with extra positive weights outside that support. Now iterate the cut calculation $n$ times; it gives a $T^+$ action on $W_n(Y)$ and hence the required $S$ action. ### A surface model retaining the braids and all label cells

Here is the stronger base comparison in scalar degree two. Use $R$ equal to published insertion, or to the full binary surface with unary disc removal. Suppose $H_D\to UY$ is a raw weak equivalence into an $R$-model. Then $H_{X_2(D)}$ is raw weakly equivalent to the reduct of an $R$-model. We give the construction because separate tests on each label and on the unlabelled configuration would lose the correlation between the braid and the output order of the labels.

For any colour set $J$ use the braided strict monoidal groupoid of words in $J$ and braids respecting endpoint colours. Regard it as a Gray-category $G_J$ with one object and one arrow. Its interchanger is the block crossing, with its two multiplicativity axioms given by the braid relations. Use the discrete order on parallel 3-cells. Put $P(J)=K(G_J)$ for insertion, or $P(J)=E(G_J)$ for the binary laws, with the operations of Responses 5 and 11. These are ordinary surface models. In the first model a 2-cell is a word. In the second it is an event history modulo the specified exchanges; an atom is labelled by a word. Its strand positions are the letters in the word obtained by evaluating the normal representative. In either model a 3-cell is an actual braid between the words at its two ends, and higher cells are identities. The history normalisation depends on the event addresses and stationary arrows, so renaming the letters preserves the normal representative. Consequently an uncoloured 2-cell can be coloured uniquely from its strand positions, even for an empty atom, and a braid can be coloured uniquely from its input. Recolouring commutes with all the operations: for histories a sort replaces an exchange by its block braid, with the same endpoint permutation after renaming. [History, triples and insertion models](#researcher-response-5) · [Disc action](#researcher-response-11) · [Baez–Neuchl, one-object Gray monoids and braided strict monoidal categories](https://math.ucr.edu/home/baez/neuchl.pdf)

The pure scalar map to $UP(1)$ sending the scalar to the singleton (a one-event history in the binary case) is a raw weak equivalence. To verify this first for $K(G_1)$, the raw double hom has one component per cardinality, with the $r$th component the unordered planar configuration space. Its fundamental group is the braid group $\mathrm{Br}_r$ and it is aspherical, by the configuration fibration. The target double hom is the braid groupoid. The induced map surjects on each fundamental group. At two scalars Rice's raw $E(a,a)$ evaluates to the elementary crossing or its inverse: the published unit equality identifies it with the generic square, and the unique Gray lift of that square on the generic two-column arity is the structural interchanger. Its evaluation is the single crossing in $G_1$. At $r$ scalars place this raw path at a chosen pair of consecutive positions by top composition of 2-cells with the other scalars stationary. Rebracket to and from one fixed raw composite of the $r$ scalars. The rebracketing comparisons for this vertical composite evaluate to identities, since their arities are in one strict Gray hom. Thus the image at this basepoint contains every adjacent braid generator up to inversion. [Unit calculation on the raw braid](#researcher-response-26) · [Planar configuration calculation](#researcher-response-36)

For precision, a surjective endomorphism of $\mathrm{Br}_r$ is injective. The group is finitely generated and residually finite: its faithful Laurent polynomial matrix representation separates a nonidentity matrix after reducing modulo a suitable prime and evaluating the invertible indeterminates in a sufficiently large finite field. For any finite group $H$, precomposition by a surjection permutes the finite set $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathrm{Br}_r,H)$, so every finite quotient kills the kernel. This proves the assertion, including the trivial groups for $r=0,1$. It follows that the map is an equivalence on each aspherical component. The lower cells are the point and its unit up to equivalence. For $E(G_1)$ use the raw span of trivial fibrations on triples from Response 5 with the comparison on the singleton atom chosen to be the identity. The generating assignment lifts to that triple, and two-out-of-three proves the same result. With a set of colours $J$ the comparisons are also equivalences. Over an uncoloured component both colourings are covers with fibre the assignments of the prescribed colours to its $r$ positions. In the raw configuration description this is the ordered cover modulo the colour stabilizer; in the groupoid descriptions it is unique path lifting of a coloured braid. At the fixed $r$-fold composite the map identifies those fibres position by position. Naturality in renaming now gives equivalence on the covers. Decorate $P(1)$ as follows. At degree two attach an object of $Y$ to each position. At degree $2+j$, $j>0$, attach a $j$-cell of $Y$ to each input strand. For $j=1$ its ends are the input label and the output label at the braid's transported position. For $j>1$ the two faces have the same braid, and the faces of the labels are taken on the same strands. The lower cells are those of $P(1)$. To apply a surface head, first evaluate its $P(1)$ component. Trace each output position back to the input arity. Along an interval of 2-slots transport by the input braid, and on different slots use distinct names for all their positions. At rank two the head uses each contributing slot once: in the insertion model it concatenates event lists in column order; in the history model it substitutes the events and sorts, transporting their letters by the sorting braid. To check this operation, colour the tuple in $P(J)$ with the fresh names just used. In every evaluated subexpression over the arity each name occurs at most once in its degree-two source: the positional arity takes at most one 2-variable from each transport string. Consequently the auxiliary tuples for a nested evaluation are exactly the tuples obtained by first evaluating for each name in $W_2(Y)$ and keeping the indicated entry. The construction with tagged positions in $P(J)$ gives the same model with tags remembered, and forgetting tags is a surface map.

Assign the generators of $X_2(D)$ by taking singleton strands with the actual images of their labels in $Y$. This gives a raw map $H_{X_2(D)}\to UV$. Here is descent to the untagged hom at exact ends. Choose an ordering at each of two objects with $r$ strands. In the source realization the mapping category is the disjoint union over permutations of the mapping categories between the corresponding tagged objects, by the simultaneous permutation orbit formula in Response 36. In the target every arrow has one braid and hence one of those permutations. All higher comparisons preserve it, and its source tags uniquely extend along the braid. After fixing the permutation, the mapping category is the one at those tagged ends: already in the raw model its operations use the same braids and strand labels, with uniquely determined tags. ## Researcher Response 38

**In an ordinary scalar 3-computad, all ten surfaces are conservative in every dimension if each generating 3-cell has exactly one scalar occurrence in its target.** The source may have any number, including zero. Repeated inputs, parallel rules and arbitrarily long chains of merges are allowed. The dual result holds if each source has one occurrence and the targets are arbitrary. Here a scalar 3-computad has one object, no generating arrows, generating 2-scalars and generating 3-cells. Counts refer to the ordinary strict top chain of the actual attaching term.

More generally, let $n\ge2$, with scalars in degree $n$ and rules in degree $n+1$, and suppose at least one scalar is present. Under the single-output hypothesis, conservativity of **each** of the ten surfaces in a given degree is equivalent to its conservativity in that degree on $B_n$. This equivalence also holds under the dual single-input hypothesis. The single-output case includes $g:a*_{n-1}a\to a$: no positive integer weight on $a$ is preserved by that rule. The proof assigns trees to individual occurrences of a derivation.

### The mapping spaces of a presentation by merges

First take standard scalar boundaries at the point. For every rule $g$ choose an enumeration of the $p_g$ scalar occurrences in its $n$-source. To interpret a source with repeated colours, first distinguish its occurrences in the pure scalar raw syntax. In the ordered configuration description this specifies a point $\alpha_g$ of $E_n(p_g)$ up to transport; use any representative. The configuration of its singleton target can likewise be transported to the unary unit. These choices describe the actual attaching map: before the rules are adjoined the $n$-fold hom is the free little-cubes algebra on the scalar colours. Moving a boundary along these paths gives an equivalent cellular pushout relative to this base. This also allows arbitrary scalar attaching writings on the point, by the boundary transport of Response 36.

Let $P$ be the ordinary free coloured symmetric operad on one operation for each $g$, with those ordered input ports and its one output colour. Give it a map $p:P\to E_n$ by $g\mapsto\alpha_g$ (for example in simplicial operads via singular complexes). In the realization of the raw computad its $n$-fold hom is the underlying category of the **relative monoidal envelope** $\operatorname{Env}_{E_n}(P)$. To verify the derived universal property, the free discrete operad used here is already built by cofibrations of simplicial operads: adjoin the colours, then attach at each profile the free corolla on $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. Identifying two input colours does not impose invariance of the operation under their transposition; the generator still has ordered ports. These pushouts compute homotopy pushouts, also for nullary corollas, since the attaching cofibrations have cofibrant domains and the stages are cofibrant. Thus mapping this presentation into an operad over $E_n$ specifies colour images and operations over the indicated points, with their full spaces of choices. For an $E_n$-monoidal category a lift over $\alpha_g$ is precisely a morphism from its $\alpha_g$-product of the input objects to the output object. By the envelope adjunction this is the mapping property of the indicated $E_n$-monoidal category. Delooping $n$ times gives exactly the pointed cellular mapping property of the raw presentation, including its directed $(n+1)$-generators. As in Response 36 one can work in $(\infty,n+1)$-categories here. [Cisinski–Moerdijk, simplicial operads](https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.1004) · [Hinich–Moerdijk, comparison including constants](https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1112/topo.70003) · [Lurie, *Higher Algebra*, Construction 2.2.4.1 and Proposition 2.2.4.9](https://www.math.ias.edu/~lurie/papers/HA.pdf#page=211) · [Delooping at the scalar base](#researcher-response-36)

An object is represented by a tuple $x$ of $r$ named input positions and a configuration $\alpha\in E_n(r)$. For a second such object $(y,\beta)$ the mapping space is
$$
 \coprod_{f:x\to y\ {\rm active\ in}\ P^\otimes}
       \operatorname{Path}_{E_n(r)}\big(\alpha,\ \beta\circ p(f)\big).
 \tag{2}
$$
Here $f$ is a rooted forest with one tree per position of $y$. Its leaves use each numbered position of $x$ exactly once; a nullary node uses no input. A tree can also be a single input wire. The map underlying an active arrow sends every input to its root, and the operations at the roots specify exactly these trees with their port orders. To derive (2), take the fibre of the relative envelope at the unique colour of $E_n$. A morphism is an arrow on the source tuples together with a commuting triangle of active operations ending at that colour. For fixed $f$ the space of triangles is the path space displayed in (2). The category of operators of the discrete free operad has discrete hom sets, yielding the coproduct. This is the homotopy-pullback computation of the fibre and thus applies after operadic fibration replacement. Fixing the actual two objects fixes their tuples in this hom calculation, including when colours repeat.

For $n=2$ every summand of (2) is homotopy discrete by asphericity of ordered planar configurations. Thus the double hom is equivalent to an ordinary category. Every raw 4-cell has a reverse and every old type in degree at least five has a raw inhabitant: after fixing its lower boundary the question above degree four is a higher globe problem in a homotopy discrete mapping space with an already specified common boundary. Transport on the raw point and the exact globe-fibre test return the terms at the original faces. Response 5 gives ordinary conservativity through degree four for all ten surfaces, proving the first assertion. Response 31 now also applies when arbitrary higher generators are attached above this 3-skeleton: if the next generating degree is $h\ge4$, all ten are conservative through $h+1$. Neither conclusion requires a bound on the number of times a rule is used. ### Reading the forest and its path separately

Repeated closed subtrees cause no ambiguity: their places are specified by root positions and ordered ports, and they use no input positions. At a generator grafting has this property; at a head propagation composes disjoint collections of graftings and rearranges their positions. This latter assertion can equivalently be checked by induction on an $(n+1)$-expression with distinct leaves on its source. Thus at degree $n+1$ a forest exists and (2) has a path in its summand by connectivity of $E_n(r)$. At degree $n+2$ both lifted raw arrows at the boundary lie in the same forest summand by uniqueness. In larger degrees their common arrow boundary already fixes the summand.

There is a raw substitution from the copies to the pure scalar context on the fresh leaves. Send a tree to a chosen composite of its leaves and use the unit for an empty list of leaves. Send an initial leaf to its singleton generator. At each copied rule, the two substituted old faces use the same multiset of leaves, so choose a connecting raw $(n+1)$-cell by the pure configuration calculation. For nonstandard lower faces use point transport at the prescribed raw boundary. All choices concern the given direction of the rule. This substitution takes a whole path space in the selected forest summand of (2) **equivalently** to the mapping space at the two images in the pure context. Indeed its input tuple consists of $r$ different singleton leaves. On the space of structural configurations of this tuple the induced map is the ordered configuration equivalence, by the generator assignment in the free-algebra formula. A morphism in the $f$-summand consists of the path from $\alpha$ to $\beta\circ p(f)$ followed by the fixed application of $f$ under $\beta$. Applying the substitution therefore sends its variable path by that configuration equivalence and then composes with the fixed image of this application. The latter is a path in the pure configuration space, and composition with a fixed path is an equivalence of path spaces, by composing with its reverse. This proves the assertion also for $r=0$, where the path space is contractible. It does not require a positive weighting on the original colours.

If the single-scalar theory is conservative, the specialized pure old boundary in degree $k\ge n+2$ has a raw filler. Indeed the specialized surface witness can be folded to $B_n$, and the high covering of Response 34 returns the raw filler to the distinct leaf colours. By the equivalence on the identified forest summand it gives a filler of the original mapping-space boundary. The exact globe-fibre test and folding the copies give the required raw term. Degrees at most $n$ use the point; degree $n+1$ was covered by forest existence. Conversely include the pure context on a chosen scalar. In (2) its mapping spaces comprise precisely the summands on its tuples whose forest consists of identity wires with their possible permutations. Each such summand maps by the same path-space formula, and introducing operations creates additional disjoint summands. Hence existence at any pure old boundary of degree at least $n+2$ reflects along the inclusion. The pure context has no failures in smaller degrees. For the single-input version take the opposite of the final $(\infty,1)$-category. On surface terms use functions from target states to source states, propagating backwards along each transport string. The rule and head checks above compare functions at an arbitrary state at that end, and the tree is grafted onto the original input. This gives the same proof at the actual face writings, without a duality assertion about a particular surface normalizer.

For example consider $m:a*_{n-1}a\to a$. The two merge orders on three inputs, fitted to the same source by the ordinary associator, have distinct forests and no raw comparison. The unrestricted classifications in Q1 and Q2 remain open. ∎
